subject: Dedicated capacity incident: tenant routing bridge, remediation & credit plan
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Juan Alvarez <juan.alvarez@kite.ai>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity incident: tenant routing bridge, remediation & credit plan

Juan / KiteAI ops team —

Short update and next steps from Redwood on the dedicated-capacity impact you saw this morning (summary first, details below):

What happened: between ~13:20–14:10 PDT some requests routed to your dedicated GPU pool experienced high queueing and 429s due to an autoscaler control-loop race that caused rapid node churn and transient placement contention for tenant routing. This primarily affected the 2 highest-throughput tenants on your pool (incl. KiteAI-prod).

What we did right away:
- Disabled the new autoscaler release and reverted to the previous stable controller (13:34 PDT).
- Applied a temporary tenant-routing bridge that pins your highest-throughput tenants to warm nodes to avoid further eviction churn.
- Manually added two reserved instances to your pool to reduce immediate queueing (14:00 PDT).

Impact: elevated latencies and intermittent 429s for ~50 minutes; we collected request traces and KV-cache state for diagnostics.

Attachments: incident_timeline.csv (minute-level events), stacktrace_samples.txt (controller logs), kpi_snapshot_0816.png (latency/tps chart).

Customer-facing remediation and timeline:
- Short-term (today): temporary pin + reserved nodes remain in place; monitoring is green as of 14:40 PDT.
- Short-to-medium (48–72h): a configuration lock to prevent controller rollouts for your pool, plus a canary patch that adds a safety gate to the autoscaler.
- Medium (2 weeks): permanent change to routing policy that isolates placement for high-throughput tenants and a postmortem with RCA and action items.

As a gesture for the outage we will issue a one-time service credit equal to 10% of your August dedicated usage (applied as a billing credit) and we will follow up with the formal postmortem and timeline by EOD tomorrow.

I will schedule a 30m sync (optional) to walk through the technical details and the remediation plan — proposed time: Tue 08/17 10:00 PDT. Please let me know if that works for you.

Apologies again for the impact. We take dedicated pool isolation seriously and will make sure this does not recur.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity incident: tenant routing bridge, remediation & credit plan

Olga — quick ops notes / root-cause sketch for the postmortem: 

Short RCA hypothesis: an autoscaler control-loop upgrade introduced a tighter reclaim interval and a race between placement and cache-warmup. Under the usual arrival distribution for KiteAI-prod we observed:
- rapid eviction decisions from the controller when transient CPU/GPU metrics hit thresholds (median hold-time < 30s),
- subsequent placement requests failing due to transient device index conflicts,
- repeated retries created placement storms that saturated the pool's scheduling queue.

Immediate fixes applied:
1) rollback controller to prior release (13:34 PDT) — rollback halted the aggressive reclaim logic.
2) tenant pinning (14:00 PDT) — we wired a per-tenant affinity tag for KiteAI-prod + kite-analytics so the scheduler avoids preempting those allocations while the controller is still under review.
3) manual reserve of 2 nodes (14:05 PDT) — helped clear request backlog.

Next ops steps (owners):
- Diego: run an extended canary (staging) with injected spike tests to validate the fix (48h).
- Grace: own customer-facing patch notes and compliance notes for their security/compliance team (24h).
- Marissa: confirm billing credit workflow and accounting entry for RDW-4721 (EOD).

I'll attach a short dump of controller logs (stacktrace_samples.txt) to the postmortem. We should include a mitigation runbook item: "pause autoscaler rolling upgrades for dedicated pools flagged as high-throughput".

Diego
Director, Platform Reliability
diego.fernandez@redwood.com

--

Pushing proposed timeline and permanent mitigations so we can confirm during the customer sync: 

Proposal (short list):
- Configuration lock for your dedicated pool: immediate, in place until canary finishes (owner: Grace; ETA: within 8 hours).
- Canary patch: add a safety gate to the autoscaler that requires a minimum warm-up window before reclaim decisions (owner: Diego; ETA: start canary within 24h, run 48h load injection).
- Per-tenant placement isolation: implement an affinity class for "high-throughput" tenants and a hard cap on evictions for those classes (owner: Platform Eng; ETA: 2 weeks).
- Monitoring: new alert that watches placement retry rate + scheduler conflict errors (owner: Observability team; ETA: 72h).
- Billing credit: Marissa to confirm the accounting flow and send the billing reference to Kite.

Operational note: the pinning we applied is a short-lived affinity override; it will not change autoscaler logic other than preventing eviction for the pinned tenant set. Other tenants should see normal autoscaling behavior, but we'll be careful to monitor headroom for the pool.

I'm drafting the technical slide for the customer sync and the postmortem doc. Diego, please attach the controller log snippets to the postmortem after the canary completes.

Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Reliability
grace.oconnor@redwood.com

Juan — thanks for the quick reply and for agreeing to the sync.

Quick answers:
1) ETA for config lock + canary: the configuration lock will be in place within 8 hours (we've already applied it to your pool). The canary will begin tomorrow 08/17 with a 48h load-injection plan; we expect initial canary results within 72 hours. I'll share a readout as soon as the first stage completes.
2) Pinning impact on other tenants: the temporary pin is an affinity override only for your high-throughput tenants; it prevents evictions for those specific allocations. Autoscaler behavior for other tenants remains unchanged, but we will monitor headroom and may keep the two reserved nodes in place until canary completes.
3) Billing reference: RDW-4721-CREDIT-0816 — Marissa will confirm the exact invoice adjustment and send a confirmation to your billing team by EOD tomorrow.

Next steps and invites:
- 08/17 10:00 PDT — 30m technical sync (invite sent). Diego and Grace will go over the canary plan and the postmortem outline.
- Postmortem doc: EOD 08/17 draft, final with action items within 5 business days.
- Credit applied: expected on the Aug billing cycle; Marissa will confirm the ledger entry.

We appreciate your patience — we know this impacted a production window and are treating it with high priority.

Best,
